Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Evaluate parcel-index during early 2026-05-04 00:00–01:00 and late 2026-05-05 00:00–01:00. Candidate build is idx-r19 and reference is idx-r18. (1) For each period report operations, terminal failures, failure percentage, and candidate traffic percentage. (2) Pool both periods and report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage per build. (3) Report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage for each period × region × operation-class × build cell. These define eight matched slices (period × region × operation class), each containing both builds. (4) Standardize each build by giving those eight slices equal weight; report both standardized failure percentages, candidate minus reference in pp, and the number of slices where candidate is worse. (5) Report period × operation-class traffic shares and failure percentages. In assessment, explain whether the time trend and pooled build comparison support the claim “expanding the candidate improved reliability.” Identify the strongest measured association and distinguish a possible root-cause hypothesis from causal identification. Do not extrapolate beyond the observed strata. Equal weighting here is the specified target population, not weighting by observed build traffic.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/q.py <<'PY'
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect('../data/current.db'); c.row_factory=sqlite3.Row
q='''with base as (select case when o.opened_at_ms<1777939200000 then 'early' else 'late' end period, r.region_code, oc.class_code, rel.build_code,o.operation_id, (select f.is_success from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) where a.operation_id=o.operation_id order by attempt_no desc limit 1)=0 fail from logical_operations o join service_routes sr using(route_id) join services s using(service_id) join subsystems su using(subsystem_id) join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=o.route_id and o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms join releases rel using(release_id) join regions r on r.region_id=ra.pool_id join operation_classes oc using(class_id) where su.subsystem_code='search' and s.service_code='parcel-index' and o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778025600000)'''
# region join actually pools
q=q.replace('join regions r on r.region_id=ra.pool_id','join worker_pools wp on wp.pool_id=ra.pool_id join regions r using(region_id)')
for title,sql in [('period', 'select period,count(*) n,sum(fail) f,100.0*sum(fail)/count(*) pct,100.0*sum(build_code="idx-r19")/count(*) traffic from base group by period'),('build','select build_code,count(*) n,sum(fail) f,100.0*sum(fail)/count(*) pct from base group by build_code'),('cells','select period,region_code,class_code,build_code,count(*) n,sum(fail) f,100.0*sum(fail)/count(*) pct from base group by 1,2,3,4'),('mix','select period,class_code,count(*) n,100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from base b2 where b2.period=base.period) traffic,100.0*sum(fail)/count(*) pct from base group by 1,2')]:
 print(title); [print(dict(x)) for x in c.execute(q+' '+sql)]
PY
python /tmp/q.py
